'''Margaret Theodora Meyer''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRAS}} (September 1862 – 27 January 1924), also known as '''Maud Meyer'''<ref name=obs>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8_QSAQAAMAAJ&q=Margaret+Theodora+Meyer |title=The Observatory: A monthly review of astronomy, Volumes 47-48 |publisher=[[Taylor and Francis]] |date=1924 |page=99}}</ref> was a [[British people|British]] [[mathematician]]. She was one of the first directors of studies in mathematics, and one of the earliest members of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=London Mathematical Society History|publisher=London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/content/history |accessdate=24 October 2012}}</ref> In 1916, she was one of the first women to be elected a fellow of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]].<ref name="Oxford"/>

==Biography==
Meyer was born in [[Strabane|Strabane, Tyrone, Ireland]], to a [[Presbyterian]] minister, Theodore Jonas Meyer, and his wife Jane Ann. She had an older brother, Sir [[William Stevenson Meyer]], who served as [[List of High Commissioners of the United Kingdom to India|first high commissioner for India]].<ref name="Oxford">{{cite ODNB|title=Meyer, Margaret Theodora (1862–1924)|url=http://www.oxforddnb.com/view/article/48681 |first1=Mary R. S. |last1=Creese |date=October 2009|doi=10.1093/ref:odnb/48681 |access-date=24 October 2012}}{{subscription required}}</ref> Meyer spent much of her childhood in Italy.  She attended the [[North London Collegiate School for Girls]], then enrolled at [[Girton College, Cambridge]] in 1879, graduating 15th [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|wrangler]] in mathematics 1882.  In 1907, she was awarded an [[ad eundem degree|ad eundem]] MA by [[Trinity College Dublin]].<ref name="Stephen2010">{{cite book|first=Barbara |last=Stephen|title=Girton College 1869–1932|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cZmebitQs_cC&pg=PA186|access-date=19 October 2012|date=17 June 2010|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-1-108-01531-8|pages=186–187}}</ref>

She taught at [[Notting Hill and Ealing High School|Notting Hill High School]], in London, from 1882 to 1888, and then became a resident lecturer in mathematics at Girton College, where she remained for 30 years. During World War I, Meyer undertook calculational work for the British [[War Office]] in her spare time. In 1918 she resigned from work at the college and worked for the British [[Air Ministry]], which related to aircraft design and construction.<ref name="Oxford"/>

Meyer had an interest in astronomy, as part of her degree concerned [[Theoretical astronomy|mathematical astronomy]]. She carried out much unpublished work on the subject.{{Citation needed|date=April 2019}} In 1916, she was one of the first women to be elected to the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] along with [[A. Grace Cook]], [[Fiammetta Wilson]], Ella Church, [[Mary Adela Blagg|Mary Blagg]] and Irene Elizabeth Toye Warner.<ref name="Oxford"/>

==Other activities==
Meyer carved, and supervised students in the carving, of the oak paneling around the chancel of the [[Girton College, Cambridge#Chapel|college chapel]] at Girton College.<ref name="Stephen2010"/> She also had a passion for mountain climbing, and was a member and later president of the [[Ladies' Alpine Club]] (1916-1919).<ref name=LAJP>{{cite journal | journal = The Journal of the Ladies' Alpine Club | date = 1975 | title= Lists of Presidents, Hon. Secretaries, Hon. Treasurers, Hon. Librarians, Hon. Editors, 1907-1975| pages = 4}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ladies Alpine Club Archive|url=http://www.alpine-club.org.uk/library/archives.html|publisher=[[Alpine Club (UK)|The Alpine Club]]|accessdate=24 October 2012|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829105506/http://www.alpine-club.org.uk/library/archives.html|archivedate=29 August 2012}}</ref> She regularly visited the [[European Alps|Alps]] to pursue her mountaineering interests; her final visit was during the 1923, only a few months before her death.<ref>{{cite journal | journal = The Journal of the Ladies' Alpine Club | date = 1975 | title= A selection of climbs by members, 1907-1974| pages = 58–72}}</ref>

==Death==
Meyer died, aged 61, in a collision with a bus, in [[Paddington]],<ref>{{cite news | date = 1 February 1924 | work = Kensington Post  |title = Tragic Accident in Porchester Terrace }}</ref> while cycling in 1924.<ref name=gaz/> In her will, she bequeathed [[£sd|£]]2000 to Girton College for the benefit of women mathematics students,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Obituary Notices : Fellows : Meyer, Margaret Theodora|bibcode=1925MNRAS..85R.314. |date=February 1925|publisher=[[Royal Astronomical Society]]/Weldon & Wesley |location=London|volume=85 |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |pages=314–315 |doi=10.1093/mnras/85.4.314|doi-access=free }} provided by SAO/NASA Astrophysics Data System (ADS) and published at Digital Library for Physics and Astronomy operated by [[Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory]] (SAO).</ref> an additional £1000, and a collection of mathematics books.<ref name="Stephen2010"/>
